conventions.convention: Barycentric support nodes are distinct complex numbers and every support weight is nonzero. Support values use the cleared quotient; poles are zeros of the denominator after cancellation of all common polynomial factors.
Floater–Hormann nodes are strictly increasing real numbers indexed 0 through n, with n≥1 and integer degree parameter 0≤d<n. Empty products equal one, and the support-weight sign is (−1)^(j−d).
The degree-zero local mesh ratio β is zero for n≤2; otherwise it is the maximum over interior gaps of the smaller ratio to the two neighboring gaps.
The parity parameter ε equals one when m=n−d is even and zero when m is odd. The error norms are uniform norms on the node hull [x₀,xₙ].

AAA uses exact arithmetic, absolute sampled-error tolerance, support budget 0≤B≤floor(N/2), and a finite QR sweep budget. Residual ties use the least original sample index; singular-subspace selection uses the first nonzero coordinate projection, normalized and phased positive at its first nonzero coordinate.

Padé matching normalizes q₀=1, assigns cₖ=0 for negative k, distinguishes inconsistent and consistent rank-deficient systems, and does not select a denominator on the nonunique branch. For n=0 it returns q=1.
Order-zero divided differences are evaluations. The Hermite–Genocchi simplex integral uses iterated Riemann integration with volume 1/q!, and order zero means evaluation with volume one.

load_bearing.statement: For n≥1 and 0≤d<n, the Floater–Hormann quotient equals both the λ-weighted local-polynomial blend and the μ-weighted blend. Clearing the node factors gives (∏ⱼ(x−xⱼ))∑ᵢλᵢ(x)=(−1)^(n−d)s(x), as a polynomial identity including the nodes; expansion gives exactly the defined barycentric weights and the assigned support values.

In an open node gap, each nonempty μ-block sum over I₁, I₂, I₃ is positive. The right block alternates starting positive with strictly decreasing magnitudes; the left block does likewise read backward; every middle-block term is positive when d≥1.
For n≥1, 0≤d<n, strictly increasing real nodes and h the largest adjacent gap, every open gap satisfies |D_d(x)|≥1/(d! h^(d+1)) when d≥1, and |D₀(x)|≥1/[h(1+β)] when d=0.

For n≥1, 0≤d<n, increasing real nodes, a query x in their hull distinct from the nodes, and f∈C^(d+1) with V=Var(f^(d+1)) finite, the adjacent window differences Gᵢ=f[xᵢ,…,xᵢ₊d,x] satisfy ∑ᵢ₌₀^(n−d−1)|Gᵢ₊₁−Gᵢ|≤V/(d+1)!.

For distinct real nodes and assigned real values, f[t₀,…,t_q]=∑ⱼ f(tⱼ)/∏ₖ≠ⱼ(tⱼ−tₖ). It is symmetric in the nodes and is the coefficient of t^q in their unique degree-at-most-q interpolating polynomial.
For the data and nonzero weights in def-barycentric-rational-quotient, Q is not the zero polynomial, P/Q is well-defined, and r(zⱼ)=fⱼ for each support node.
For any n≥1, any distinct ordered real nodes x₀<⋯<xₙ, any real data f₀,…,fₙ, and any integer 0≤d<n, the exact Floater–Hormann rational function has no real poles.

At an AAA iteration whose exact SVD call completes successfully, the selected unit weight vector minimizes the Loewner residual over unit vectors, with residual equal to the smallest singular value. Nonzero selected weights and no pole-status return give support interpolation. The procedure terminates after at most B iterations; no minimax or uniform off-grid convergence is asserted.

For a power series convergent on |z|<R, R>0, any normalized solution of the full Padé moment equations with the stated convolution numerator satisfies f(z)−p(z)/q(z)=O(z^(m+n+1)) as z→0. No pole-location or analytic-continuation guarantee follows.

published_dependencies.used_for: Real cardinal Lagrange formulas, including empty products and sorted distinct nodes.
Existence and uniqueness of the interpolating polynomials used in divided-difference leading coefficients, window interpolation and the Newton remainder.
Order-zero cases and natural-number derivative and interpolation orders.
Induction proving the divided-difference Lagrange formula and the Hermite–Genocchi identity and simplex volume.
C^q regularity, recursive derivatives and one-sided endpoint conventions.
Finiteness of continuous derivative norms and continuous errors on nonempty compact intervals.
Repeated Rolle applications giving the divided-difference derivative bound.
Integration of the inner derivative and of simplex sections in the Hermite–Genocchi proof.
Full right singular bases, kernel directions and minimization of the unit-vector Loewner residual.
The exact bidiagonal reduction called by AAA and the explicit transfer-function example.
AAA's finite-budget exact SVD call, zero deflation tolerance, shift tie rule and deflation-before-budget behavior.
The partition-supremum definition controlling monotone simplex-window samples and the BV error estimate.
Checking the explicit real Givens factor in the one-sweep transfer-function example.
The signed-norm Householder reductions and unitary equivalence used in that example.
